1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust upward by 2–5% for the first 5–10 days.

2. Model exhibits strong upward bias after sharp price spikes — reduce forecast by 3–8% for the 3–7 day period following a spike.

3. Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window — increase forecast by 1–3% for days 10–20 if recent prices are above 30-day average.

4. Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — reduce forecast by 2–6% for the last 5–10 days, especially if true prices show downward momentum.

5. Model shows persistent lag in responding to new data — add 1–3 days of delay in forecast adjustment when true prices deviate from model by >3% from prior day.

6. Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes — increase forecast by 1–4% for days when true prices are below 65–70% of 30-day average.

7. Model overfits to recent high prices — reduce forecast by 2–5% if the last 5 days are above 80% of 30-day average.

8. Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar effects — increase forecast by 1–3% for days near end of month or during high-demand periods (e.g., EU ETS auction days).
